questions.q: How are the dashboards in Data Estate Insights produced, per the lesson?
options: A data steward builds each one manually in Power BI
They require a separate paid add-on to activate
They're automatically generated and populated from the Data Map's scanned metadata
They're hand-written quarterly by Microsoft support
questions.explain: As Purview scans and populates the Data Map, the Data Estate Insights application automatically extracts and surfaces governance gaps — nobody builds these reports by hand.

questions.q: What are the three sections every Data Estate Insights report falls under?
options: Health, Inventory and ownership, Curation and governance
Scanning, Classification, Labeling
Collections, Domains, Glossary
Ingestion, Transformation, Consumption
questions.explain: Every report falls under Health, Inventory and ownership, or Curation and governance.

questions.q: In the current Microsoft Purview portal, where do the same reports described in this lesson now live?
options: They were discontinued entirely
Only inside the classic Azure portal, with no current-portal equivalent
Inside Microsoft Fabric exclusively
Inside Data Catalog, under Data Estate Health > Reports
questions.explain: The classic portal called this application Data Estate Insights; the current portal moved the same reports into Data Catalog under Data Estate Health > Reports.

questions.q: What does the Data Stewardship dashboard's "Data estate health" table show, per the lesson?
options: A single org-wide percentage with no further detail
The same curation/ownership/classification metrics broken down per collection
A list of every individual user's login history
Billing information for the Purview account
questions.explain: The Data estate health table breaks curation, ownership, and classification metrics down per collection, so a steward can identify which specific collection is dragging the overall number down.

questions.q: What happens if a Health Management Action is marked Resolved, but the underlying catalog issue is actually still there?
options: Nothing — the action stays marked Resolved permanently
The entire Purview account is flagged for an audit
The next scheduled health-management refresh reopens the action automatically
The assigned owner is automatically removed from all roles
questions.explain: Resolution isn't taken on faith — the next scheduled refresh re-checks the catalog, and the action reopens automatically if the issue hasn't actually been fixed.
